title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the 2020 Committee report on AI and public standards by outlining its policy priorities, including stronger regulation, greater public trust, and responsible AI development. It announces measures such as updated guidelines, enhanced oversight mechanisms, and collaboration with industry and civil society to ensure AI aligns with societal values and protects citizens.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting rules to guide how artificial intelligence can be used in exams and qualifications. This approach was created after a request from three top government ministers to keep testing fair, reliable, and safe.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how AI systems use copyrighted material and looks at the legal and ethical implications of that use. It offers guidance for policymakers and industry stakeholders on how to develop AI responsibly while respecting copyright laws.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government outlines its plan to respond to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It commits to strengthening regulation, boosting investment in research, ensuring safety and fairness, and fostering international cooperation to keep the UK at the forefront of AI innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope, objectives, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with and impacts public standards, including a clear set of terms of reference. It also provides FAQs to help stakeholders understand the committee’s role in ensuring AI systems meet established public norms and regulations.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence, outlining its views on regulation and oversight. The submission aims to inform the committee’s policy recommendations for responsible AI development and use.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy outlines how AI will shape the regulatory framework for medical products, focusing on safety, efficacy, and data integrity. It emphasizes implementing the AI White Paper principles to ensure responsible and transparent use of AI in medical product development and oversight.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines the government's plan to integrate AI across the defence sector. It aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential in AI for its size.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will use AI to improve transport services and infrastructure. It explains how the department will partner with the transport sector to maximise benefits while putting safeguards in place to manage safety, privacy and ethical risks.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyrighted materials are used in training AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights current practices, challenges, and recommendations for balancing copyright protection with AI innovation.
